_comment:
Diet engine quality baseline. Re-recorded because CANDIDATE ORDERING was wrong and the template shortlist was too short. Two defects, one visible effect. (1) CandidatePool added a structure score (meal-library membership, macro role, cuisine, density) to a preference score, and the structure half was unbounded: a food that matched several structural rules out-scored an explicit like. STRUCTURE_CEILING was meant to cap it and did not, because it capped each term rather than the sum. The fix scales the whole structure component down proportionally once the widest one exceeds the ceiling, so an explicit choice always outranks a merely well-fitting food. (2) diet/planner/templates.py hardcoded a 12-food shortlist per slot; with the corrected ordering that window was too narrow and staples the client had chosen (chicken breast, beef mince, chickpeas, broccoli) could not be reached at all. SHORTLIST is now a named constant at 20, chosen by measurement:
  variant                    dish    distinct  chosen  pref    drift  repeats
  previous baseline          0.8036  60        0.3066  0.6875  3.330  7
  bounded ordering, cap 12   0.8690  61        0.2313  0.6250  2.809  7
  bounded ordering, cap 20   0.8929  65        0.2411  0.6875  2.181  6
  bounded ordering, cap 30   0.8690  61        0.2409  0.6875  2.890  7
Kept at 20: dish rate 0.804 -> 0.893, distinct dishes 60 -> 65, worst calorie drift 3.33 -> 2.18, weekly repeats of one dish 7 -> 6, preference satisfaction unchanged at 0.6875. The price is chosen-ingredient share 0.3066 -> 0.2411, and it is a real cost recorded deliberately: the old number was inflated by the same unbounded structure score that let a handful of well-connected foods dominate every plate, so a larger share of components came from a smaller set of the client's likes. The new plans reach more of the catalogue, portion closer to target, and repeat less. Earlier deliberate trades still hold: a substitution may not replace the ingredient a dish is named after, and min_distinct_portions_per_food is measured over engine-BUILT plates only, because a recipe author's pinned clove of garlic is meant to be identical every time. The catalogue-lookup defect this file was previously re-recorded for (FoodCategory.by_canonical_name resolving to None under modeltranslation, 86 of 136 foods uncategorised) is fixed and its numbers are superseded by the table above.
